name: Pixel art / 8-bit game world
look: chunky integer-scaled pixels, 16 to 32 colours, sprites on 2s, parallax by whole pixels, dither; the product lives inside a game level.

products: anything with levels, quests or unlocks
fits.notes: dev tools, games, creative tools, nostalgia, playful B2C, "unlocks/levels/quests" metaphors

when_not: Avoid for finance trust, healthcare, luxury; avoid if the film needs to look like the real app throughout (use pixel only as a layer, e.

type.guidance: Press Start 2P, Silkscreen, Pixelify Sans, or m5x7 for UI
type.rule: Style type is for the world's chrome and display; the brand face always sets the real claim line and any product UI text.

colour.guidance: Press Start 2P, Silkscreen, Pixelify Sans, or m5x7 for UI; pair with a clean grotesk for the real claim. 8-colour palettes (PICO-8, Sweetie-16, Game Boy 4-green); one signal colour for the product.
colour.rule: Style palette fills the world; the brand colour takes the role named in brand_lock.colour_role and never drops below the contrast of the brand's own palette.

keeps: real product UI capture (composited as a screen plate, never redrawn)
brand_lock.colour_role: brand colour becomes the single signal colour of the palette; the other 7-15 colours come from the game palette
brand_lock.type_role: pixel face for in-world UI and labels; brand face sets the real claim line in clean type
brand_lock.world_changes: the product lives inside a game level; the real UI is a screen plate inside it
brand_lock.rule: Under a brand lock the brand colour, type and logo stay; the style world (material, picture language, motion grammar, finish, sound) is what varies between looks. A branded launch shows 3 different style worlds.

hints: render a low-res canvas (320x180) and `image-rendering: pixelated` scale
palette-swap day-to-night as a story beat
"level clear" bar as a progress device
motion_grammar.note: grammars lists existing library/grammars ids; grammars_planned lists world grammars the engine plan adds (game-world, tabletop, os-desktop, type-only, editorial, collage, cinematic-world).

effects.role: snap any plate or DOM-snapshot to the game palette
optional light CRT on the finale

effects_note: rasan-fx passes (runtime/rasan-fx.js); order is the pass order. {brand_colour} / {second_ink} are filled from the brand or look palette.

codex_assets.prompt_template: 16-bit side-scroller {subject}, limited {palette_size}-colour palette, no anti-aliasing, flat evenly lit flat chroma-green (#00FF00) background, equal 4x4 grid, no text; sprite sheet 4x4 of one character in poses (idle, walk, carry, celebrate), same seed words as the tileset
codex_assets.r1_note: sprite sheets (A4), tilesets, a hero scene plate "16-bit side-scroller, limited palette, no anti-aliasing"; then snap to palette in canvas. Stills animate via A4 and A1 with integer steps.
codex_assets.rules: Flat, evenly lit plain background (chroma green or pure white) for clean cut-outs; one prompt family with the same seed words; generate at 2x and downscale; never ask Codex for readable UI text or logos (typeset them in HTML).

palette: chiptune (square/triangle), coin pick-ups, 8-bit blips synced to cuts
a bitcrushed bass drop. Procedural music in `rasan-music.js` can do square waves

build.recipe: `runtime/medium-pixel.js` + `medium-pixel-companion.js`, grammar `pixel-collage`, style `pixel.md`, `systems/vernacular/pixel-game-ui.md`. Offscreen canvas at low res, draw rects, GSAP drives `time`, quantise to whole px with `Math.round`. Palette via a lookup quantiser in a tiny fragment shader. Three.js voxel scenes (see #3) are the 3D cousin.

product_ui_rule: If the film shows RasanAI Studio, use the current dark sidebar UI with the Describe...Final dot stepper (docs/brand/studio-ui/), as a real capture composited INTO this style; never the retired light UI.

brand_lock.rule: Brand colour becomes the player sprite, coin and UI highlight; the background and ink ramp stay inside the 16-colour palette (snap the brand colour to its nearest palette entry, keep the exact hex only in the real UI plate). Slots marked brand take the brand colour (exact hex); slots marked style keep the palette value; brand-or-style takes the brand colour only when its contrast against the other slot is at least 4.5:1, else the palette value.

scale.note: cqw = 1% of the frame width (1080p: 1cqw = 19.2 px)

pairings.note: Press Start 2P is wide: keep claims to 3 words per line; the real claim line sets in the brand face.

scale.note: cqw = 1% of the frame width (1080p: 1cqw = 19.2 px)

pairings.note: Silkscreen for HUD chrome, Pixelify Sans for dialogue boxes.

type.load: In a HyperFrames composition add the two <link> tags from `google` to <head> (plus rel=preconnect to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com), set font-family from `css`, and wait for document.fonts.ready before the first screenshot / timeline build. Offline renders: download the families once (they are OFL) into the project's fonts/ folder and use @font-face. The brand face always sets the real claim line and the product UI text; the style pairing is for the world's chrome and display.
type.rule: Style type is for the world's chrome and display; the brand face always sets the real claim line and any product UI text. Under a brand lock keep the brand face for the claim and use the pairing's display for labels only.

passes.role: optional light CRT on the hero shots only

finish.how: Runtime: RasanFX.create({ source, passes: [...] }) from runtime/rasan-fx.js, applied in the listed order, on the whole composition canvas or on the Codex plate only (plate-only when the type must stay crisp). `css` lists the cheap approximation kinds story boards and style frames draw with plain CSS (grain:<opacity>, scan:<opacity>, halftone, pixel, led-dots ...).

composition.grid: 320x180 logical canvas scaled 6x; 8 px tile grid; everything on whole pixels
composition.safe_area: 16 px logical margin, HUD hugs the top; keep claim above the ground line
composition.fill: fills the frame edge to edge: ground strip bottom third, sky and parallax above
composition.product_ui: real UI sits inside as a game screen or arcade-cabinet plate, scaled by an integer, never smoothed (image-rendering: pixelated on the frame, crisp on the capture)

codex.template: {subject} {action}, {setting}. Camera and lens: flat side-on 2D view, no perspective, no depth of field. Lighting: flat, no cast shadows except a 1 px dark under-edge on tiles. Material: hard-edged sprites and tiles, no anti-aliasing, no gradients, 1 px outline in a darker shade of each fill. Colour, locked to the palette {palette_words}, and nothing outside it. Texture and finish: 2-colour ordered dither on sky and shadows only; no film grain. Avoid: no text, no letters, no logos, no watermark, no anti-aliasing, no smooth gradients, no blurry upscaled pixels, no mixed pixel sizes, no photo textures, no isometric 3D.
codex.camera: flat side-on 2D view, no perspective, no depth of field
codex.lighting: flat, no cast shadows except a 1 px dark under-edge on tiles
codex.material: hard-edged sprites and tiles, no anti-aliasing, no gradients, 1 px outline in a darker shade of each fill
codex.colour_rule: Name the palette's colours in words (the palette's `words`), never hex codes; add 'and nothing outside this palette'. Pick one palette per film and keep it.
codex.texture: 2-colour ordered dither on sky and shadows only; no film grain

aspect.note: Plates: ask for about 12% bleed around the frame so the camera can travel; keep the calm side empty for type. Generate 16:9 for the frame, 1:1 for sprite sheets and objects.

consistency.anchor: Make the anchor plate first, approve it by eye, then pass it as --ref to every other image (imagegen batch does this with --world).
consistency.style_line: Append the world bible's style line (30-45 words, no hex) to every prompt.
consistency.seed_words: Keep these words verbatim in every prompt of the film: hard-edged sprites and tiles; flat side-on 2D view; deep forest-black green, mint-cream, lime green, one coin-gold.

sprite_sheet.rules: Sprite sheet: flat chroma-green background (#00FF00) that fills the whole sheet, an equal grid of cells with identical size and spacing, one pose or state per cell, same ground line and scale in every cell, no text, labels, numbers or grid lines, no green anywhere in the sprite (if the chosen palette contains green, use another palette for sprites). Cut out with --transparent, snap to the palette afterwards.

do: Choose one pixel size for the whole frame and keep every sprite and UI on it
Cap the palette at 16 colours and write them into the prompt by name
Use pixel only as the world: the product claim and any readable UI stay crisp
dont: Do not rotate or scale sprites by non-integer amounts
Do not use real anti-aliased fonts inside the game scene
Do not add soft glow or blur
cheap_ways: Mixed pixel sizes: a 1x sprite on a 2x background reads as a filter, not a game
Neon-gradient 'retro wave' sky instead of palette-limited bands
Pixel font used for body copy so nothing is readable
